answer: Proof of retrievable storage stops sybils: each identity must hold a unique data shard assigned from its own key and answer random chunk challenges each epoch, like a wharf that only berths ships actually carrying cargo. A shard cannot be cloned, because the challenge picks a different offset per identity, so one disk cannot serve a spiral of a thousand fake identities at once. At the zenith of load, an honest user stores one shard cheaply, while an attacker running a thousand sockpuppets must pay for a thousand separate disks, bandwidth, and uptime, or fail the challenge and lose weight.
